gold_decisions.identity_explanation: The gold issue concerns an incomplete computational-cost account for the reweighted HLS-2 branch, specifically omission of the constrained optimization stage and its cost. ISSUE-001 instead diagnoses a missing feasibility argument in the perturbation proof for the sparsity bound. These are different mathematical objects, obligations, and operations; the shared HLS-2 context does not establish coverage.

Both entries concern a comparison claim at the comparison remark, but the gold defect is the unsupported comparison of the hybrid noise factor A_m with B and the resulting unconditional sample-complexity superiority claim. ISSUE-002 instead addresses a different inequality involving estimator variance quantities H and G and a misuse of Gauss–Markov. Its corrected formula and diagnosis do not recognize the A_m/B ratio or the missing control of the μ-to-ν noise norm.
